statement: The command tally shall report how long each text file that the user names is, measured as its number of lines, words and characters.
criterion: Given a text file of 3 lines, 6 words and 30 characters, running tally on it prints the counts 3, 6 and 30 for that file.

statement: The command tally shall read each file that the user names and print, for each file, its number of lines, words and characters, and shall print a total of those counts.
criterion: Given two text files with known counts, tally prints one row per file with its lines, words and characters, and a final row whose counts are the sums of the two files' counts.

statement: The command shall be invoked as tally [-l] [-w] [-c] [file...] and shall accept zero or more file names.
criterion: Running tally with zero, one and three file names, with and without each of the flags -l, -w and -c, is accepted and produces counts; each named file appears in the output.

statement: The flag -l shall select the line count, -w the word count and -c the character count; with no flag, tally shall print all three counts.
criterion: For a file with known counts, tally -l prints only the line count, tally -w only the word count, tally -c only the character count, and tally with no flag prints the line, word and character counts.

statement: When no file name is given, tally shall read and count standard input.
criterion: Piping a text with known counts into tally with no file name prints the line, word and character counts of that text, and the exit code is 0.

statement: The output shall have one row for each file, holding the counts that the flags select followed by the file name, each field separated from the next by exactly one space; with two files or more, a last row named total shall hold the sum of each selected count.
criterion: For one file, the output is exactly one row of the form '<counts> <name>' with single spaces; for two files, the output is two file rows followed by a row ending in 'total' whose counts are the sums; with -w, each row holds only the word count and the name.

statement: When a named file cannot be read, tally shall write a message to standard error that holds the file name and the reason, and shall end with exit code 1.
criterion: Running tally on a file that does not exist, and on a file without read permission, writes to standard error a message holding that file name and the reason (such as no such file or permission denied), and the exit code is 1.

statement: A file that cannot be read shall not stop the counting of the other named files.
criterion: Running tally on a readable file, then a missing file, then a second readable file prints the rows of both readable files with correct counts, writes the error for the missing file to standard error, and exits with code 1.

statement: When a file is not valid UTF-8, tally shall write a message to standard error that holds the file name, and shall end with exit code 1.
criterion: Running tally on a file that holds an invalid UTF-8 byte sequence (such as the byte 0xFF) writes to standard error a message holding that file name, and the exit code is 1.

statement: When no error occurs, tally shall end with exit code 0.
criterion: Running tally on readable, valid UTF-8 files, and on valid standard input, ends with exit code 0.

statement: The product shall be written in Go, using only the Go standard library, and shall be built with the Go toolchain.
criterion: The go.mod file declares no required module, every import is a standard-library package, and go build succeeds with the Go toolchain alone.

statement: The product shall count only lines, words and characters, and shall offer no other count such as bytes, paragraphs or sentences.
criterion: The usage accepts only the flags -l, -w and -c; any other flag, such as one for bytes, paragraphs or sentences, is rejected and no such count is printed.

statement: The product shall not read archives, directories or files that are not text.
criterion: No code path unpacks an archive or walks a directory; naming a directory does not produce counts of its contents.

statement: The product shall be a command-line program only, with no graphical interface, network service or plug-in system.
criterion: The source imports no graphical, network-server or plug-in package (such as net/http or plugin), and the program opens no window and no listening socket.

statement: A line shall be a run of characters that ends with a line feed; the last line of a file shall count as a line when the file does not end with a line feed.
criterion:
The text 'a
b
' counts 2 lines, 'a
b' counts 2 lines, '' counts 0 lines and '
' counts 1 line.

statement: A word shall be a run of characters that are not white space, where white space is any character with the Unicode property White_Space.
criterion: The text 'one  two\tthree' counts 3 words; text separated by U+00A0 NO-BREAK SPACE or U+3000 IDEOGRAPHIC SPACE splits into separate words; a text of only white space counts 0 words.

statement: A character shall be one Unicode code point of a text in UTF-8, whatever the number of bytes that encode it.
criterion: The text 'aé€😀' (1, 2, 3 and 4 bytes per code point) counts 4 characters; a combining sequence such as 'e' followed by U+0301 counts 2 characters.

statement: Counting a file of 10 MiB shall take at most 2 seconds on a computer with 4 cores.
criterion: A test that counts a generated file of 10 MiB (10,485,760 bytes) measures an elapsed time of at most 2 seconds on a computer with 4 cores.

statement: Counting a file of 1 GiB shall use at most 64 MiB of heap.
criterion: A test that counts a generated file of 1 GiB (1,073,741,824 bytes) reads a heap size of at most 64 MiB (67,108,864 bytes) at the end.

statement: The tests of the counting package shall cover at least 90 percent of its statements.
criterion: The output of go test -cover for the counting package reports a coverage of at least 90.0 percent of statements.
